Short answer: Square can fit a simpler counter or mixed retail operation. Toast is built around restaurant workflows. The right choice depends on service style, kitchen flow, order channels, hardware, payment terms, and support.

What this means for your business

A POS change touches the busiest five minutes of the night. A feature list matters less than whether servers, kitchen staff, managers, online orders, and closeout agree.

What to watch

  • A demo that skips Friday-night volume.
  • Online orders retyped into the kitchen.
  • Hardware, payment, support, or contract terms left out of the quote.
  • No documented offline or outage procedure.

Do this next

  1. Map dine-in, bar, takeout, delivery, and closeout.
  2. Run the ten ugliest orders in each demo.
  3. Compare the complete quote and contract, not a headline price.
  4. Test offline steps and train staff before cutover.

When Little Fight fits

We help restaurants document the flow, compare the real terms, set up the network, and connect the customer path. We do not sell either POS.
